::: {.callout-note}
## A bridge deck (module capstone)
This synthesis connects the popgen statistics we've built ($H$, $F_{ST}$, $F$, kinship) to
the **phenotypic** variation that selection and breeding act on — the gateway to
**quantitative genetics** (Falconer & Mackay; AGRO-931). It has no dedicated schedule day;
use it as an end-of-module synthesis or exam review. Depth here is **key results + intuition**,
not full derivations.
:::

## Where we are

- All module long we measured **genetic** variation: heterozygosity $H$, diversity $\pi$,
  differentiation $F_{ST}$, inbreeding $F$, kinship.
- But selection, adaptation, and plant breeding act on **phenotypes** — height, flowering
  time, yield.
- **Today:** how the *same* quantities map onto **phenotypic variance**, and why our popgen
  statistics predict a population's response to selection.

## Learning objectives

By the end you should be able to:

- Decompose a genotypic value into **breeding value + dominance deviation**.
- Define the **average effect** $\alpha$, additive variance $V_A$, and heritability $h^2$.
- Explain why **heterozygosity is the fuel for selection** ($V_A = 2pq\,\alpha^2$).
- Connect $F_{ST}\leftrightarrow Q_{ST}$, **kinship → heritability**, and $F$ → inbreeding
  depression.

# The genotype–phenotype map {.center}

## Genotypic values

For a single biallelic locus affecting a quantitative trait, assign **genotypic values**
around the midpoint:

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\text{genotype} & A_1A_1 & A_1A_2 & A_2A_2 \\ \hline
\text{value} & +a & d & -a
\end{array}
$$

- $a$ = additive effect; $d$ = **dominance** deviation ($d=0$: additive; $d=a$: full dominance).
- Population mean (under HW): $\;\mu = a(p-q) + 2pq\,d$.

## Average effect & breeding value

What a parent **transmits** is alleles, not genotypes. The **average effect of an allele
substitution**:

$$
\alpha = a + d(q - p).
$$

Partition each genotypic value into transmissible + non-transmissible parts:

$$
G = \mu + \underbrace{A}_{\text{breeding value}} + \underbrace{D}_{\text{dominance deviation}} .
$$

- The **breeding value** $A$ = sum of the average effects of an individual's alleles — the
  part that responds to selection and passes to offspring.

## Partitioning the variance

Phenotype adds environment: $P = G + E$. The variances partition (with
$\mathrm{Cov}(A,D)=0$ under random mating):

$$
V_P = V_A + V_D + V_E, \qquad
V_A = 2pq\,\alpha^2, \qquad
V_D = (2pq\,d)^2 .
$$

::: {.callout-important}
Note $V_A = 2pq\,\alpha^2$ **depends on allele frequency** (via $2pq$) — the additive variance
a population presents to selection is set by its **genetic diversity**, not just gene action.
:::

# Four bridges to what we already measured {.center}

## Bridge 1 — heterozygosity *is* evolvability

The $2pq$ in $V_A$ is exactly the **expected heterozygosity** $H$ from deck 01:

$$
V_A = 2pq\,\alpha^2 = H\,\alpha^2 .
$$

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="58%"}
- **More heterozygosity ⟹ more additive variance ⟹ more response to selection.**
- Anything that lowers $H$ lowers evolvability: **small $N_e$**, **bottlenecks**, and
  **selfing** <span class="xref">(decks 01, 03)</span>.
- Drift erodes $V_A$ at the **same rate** it erodes $H$:
  $\;V_{A,t} \approx V_{A,0}\left(1-\tfrac{1}{2N_e}\right)^{t}.$
:::

selfing rate; e.g. $V_A$ vs. $H$ across populations.

## Heritability & the breeder's equation

Only the **additive** part is reliably transmitted, so we distinguish:

$$
H^2 = \frac{V_G}{V_P}\ \text{(broad-sense)}, \qquad
h^2 = \frac{V_A}{V_P}\ \text{(narrow-sense)} .
$$

The response to selection — the **breeder's equation**:

$$
R = h^2\,S \qquad (\text{response} = \text{narrow-sense } h^2 \times \text{selection differential}).
$$

- $h^2$ (not $H^2$) predicts response, because parents pass **alleles**, not genotypes.
- Fitness-related traits tend to have **low $h^2$** — selection has already used up their
  additive variance <span class="xref">(the efficacy-of-selection theme, deck 04/05)</span>.

## Bridge 2 — $F_{ST}$ and its phenotypic twin $Q_{ST}$

$Q_{ST}$ is the **quantitative-trait analog of $F_{ST}$** — differentiation in a trait's
*additive* variance among populations:

$$
Q_{ST} = \frac{V_{A,\text{between}}}{V_{A,\text{between}} + 2\,V_{A,\text{within}}} .
$$

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
Under **neutral drift**, $\;\mathbb E[Q_{ST}] = F_{ST}$. So comparing them tests for selection
on the trait:

- $Q_{ST} > F_{ST}$ ⟹ **divergent** selection (local adaptation).
- $Q_{ST} \approx F_{ST}$ ⟹ consistent with drift.
- $Q_{ST} < F_{ST}$ ⟹ **stabilizing** (uniform) selection.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.figure-prompt}

selection) vs. the neutral $F_{ST}$ band.
:::

## Bridge 3 — kinship builds heritability

The genetic **covariance between relatives** is built from the **same kinship coefficient**
$f_{XY}$ we defined via IBD in deck 03:

$$
\mathrm{Cov}_G(X,Y) = 2 f_{XY}\,V_A + \Delta_{XY}\,V_D,
\qquad
\mathrm{Cov}(\text{parent},\text{offspring}) = \tfrac12 V_A .
$$

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="58%"}
- Relatives resemble each other **in proportion to their kinship** — that's how $V_A$ and
  $h^2$ are *estimated* (parent–offspring regression, sib designs, the animal model).
- The IBD/coancestry machinery from deck 03 **is** the engine of quantitative genetics.
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}

## Bridge 4 — inbreeding depression

Inbreeding coefficient $F$ (deck 03) lowers heterozygosity — and, when dominance is
**directional** (deleterious recessives, $d>0$ on average), lowers the **mean**:

$$
\Delta M \;\approx\; -\,2F\sum_{\text{loci}} p q\, d \qquad (\text{inbreeding depression}).
$$

- $F$ also **redistributes variance**: within inbred lines $V_A$ falls; **among** lines it
  rises ($2F V_A$) — why breeders use RILs/inbred lines.
- Plant relevance: selfers suffer (or have **purged**) depression; crossing inbred lines
  recovers it as **heterosis / hybrid vigor**. <span class="xref">(decks 03, 06)</span>

# Summary {.center}

## Genetic variation → phenotypic variation

| We measured (popgen) | It sets (quant gen) |
|---|---|
| heterozygosity $H = 2pq$ | additive variance $V_A = H\alpha^2$ → response $R=h^2S$ |
| differentiation $F_{ST}$ | trait differentiation $Q_{ST}$ (selection test) |
| kinship $f_{XY}$ (IBD) | resemblance $\mathrm{Cov}_G = 2f_{XY}V_A + \dots$ → $h^2$ |
| inbreeding $F$ | inbreeding depression; heterosis |

- The statistics of **genetic** variation are the statistics of **evolvability**.
- This is the doorway to **quantitative genetics & plant breeding**
  [@falconer1996; @lynchwalsh1998]; $Q_{ST}$–$F_{ST}$ is its evolutionary test
  [@spitze1993; @leinonen2013].
